text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000108 bills 99215 well above expectation in every complexity stratum, but the few returned charts support the billed level, so the case is unresolved until more records are reviewed.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevation is not explained by a sicker panel: the by-complexity table shows this provider's 99215 share running roughly three to four times the all-provider share in every stratum, including patients with zero chronic conditions billed for rashes, back pain and UTIs (for example C0073392, C0073472, C0073136). That pattern is consistent with upcoding. Against it, all 8 documented 99215 claims were supported at high MDM, including the low-complexity claim C0074107. But 8 charts, about 2% of claims returned, is too thin to clear or confirm the pattern. Some note signals suggest templating, not proof of it: about a fifth of returned notes repeat the same recorded time, 2 notes claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line, and no audit trail was received to check for cloned or bulk-created notes. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims and check whether the documented high MDM reflects the visit or a reused template. The audit trail would show how and when those notes were created."}
